title: Hit the Gym: Accelerating Query Execution to Efficiently Bootstrap Behavior Models for Self-Driving Database Management Systems
note: accelerated training-data collection for self-driving DBMS behaviour models on PostgreSQL

title: Balancing Analysis Time and Bug Detection: Daily Development-friendly Bug Detection in Linux
note: LLVM-based bug checker that runs entirely in user space with an explicit analysis-time versus bugs-found tradeoff, an obvious target for improvement; compiling the Linux source as input needs no root. Concern: program analysis rather than a resource-management topic, so topic fit is a judgement call

title: Towards VM Rescheduling Optimization Through Deep Reinforcement Learning
note: Reinforcement learning policy for VM rescheduling evaluated on released industrial traces in a simulator; no cluster needed and one GPU is ample for the policy network. Concern - only that the trace dataset download should be confirmed; inference-time budget is the paper's own metric so it is measurable with wall-clock timers

title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
note: Proximity is an LSH-based approximate key-value cache in front of a RAG vector database - squarely a cache admission/eviction/approximation policy study, and the clearest single-node fit in the venue. Rust implementation, MMLU and MedRAG benchmarks, embedding model and a 7-8B generator both fit in 24 GB FP16. Rust is not installed but rustup into $HOME needs no root. Concern: the MedRAG corpus plus index is a multi-tens-of-GB download against ~257 GB free.

title: Paralegal: Practical Static Analysis for Privacy Bugs
note: Rust static analyzer (PDG extraction + policy checking); entirely user-space, CPU-only, with a Zenodo artifact DOI and Available + Functional + Reproduced badges. Concerns: needs a pinned Rust nightly toolchain plus rustc internals (installable via rustup into $HOME); the eight evaluated applications are large Rust codebases whose builds are long but single-machine.

title: UpFuzz: Detecting Data Format Incompatibility Bugs during Distributed Storage System Upgrade
note: Upgrade-path fuzzing for distributed storage systems (Cassandra, HDFS class) driven by data-format properties of persisted state - runs as local multi-process clusters, CPU and disk only. Concern - each upgrade test is expensive so a 10-week budget limits the campaign length.

title: POD-Attention: Unlocking Full Prefill-Decode Overlap for Faster LLM Inference
note: POD-Attention is a single fused CUDA attention kernel that overlaps prefill and decode - single GPU, FlashAttention-2 style so Ampere is fine; artifact lives in the vAttention repo under pod_attn

title: Translytical Processing via DB-OS Co-designed Buffer: Cross-Engine Isolation and Tunable Update Visibility for HTAP
note: DB-OS co-designed buffer virtualization using huge-page-backed segments remapped read-only between PostgreSQL and DuckDB - implemented as a user-level library - concern: explicit huge pages normally need root, only transparent huge pages are available here - no repo located

title: Centrum: Model-based Database Auto-tuning with Minimal Distributional Assumptions
note: Model-based DBMS auto-tuning; single-node tuning loop

title: Syno: Structured Synthesis for Neural Operators
note: Automatic synthesis of new neural operators with a guided search plus tensor-compiler backend - single-GPU search and evaluation; a separate artifact repo (Yongqi-Zhuo/Syno-AE) also exists. MERGE NOTE: the same paper (identical title and DOI 10.1145/3676642.3736118) is also row 21 of the asplos-2026 report, which notes it was published in ASPLOS 2025 Volume 3 and presented at ASPLOS 2026; the asplos-2026 row was folded into this one. That scout's text: "Structured synthesis of neural operators; search plus single-GPU kernel evaluation. Published in ASPLOS 2025 Volume 3 and presented at ASPLOS 2026."

title: Osprey: Transparent and Efficient Virtual Memory for Secure Computation
note: A user-space, runtime virtual-memory layer that pages secure-computation working sets to SSD transparently - user-space memory management plus NVMe, no trusted hardware needed (this is MPC, not TEE). Concern: MPC parties are usually processes on separate hosts; they would have to be co-located as local processes

title: WISK: A Workload-aware Learned Index for Spatial Keyword Queries
note: Workload-aware learned index for spatial keyword queries - a learned index, CPU only, arXiv preprint available. Concern: no official code repository found via GitHub or web search

title: DeXOR: Enabling XOR in Decimal Space for Streaming Lossless Compression of Floating-point Data
note: Streaming lossless floating-point compression framework; small self-contained user-space codec ideal for a 10-week improvement project

title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
note: Symbolic-property analysis of DRL agents used inside systems - video streaming, wireless allocation, congestion control. Pure user-space Python plus DNN verification backends such as Marabou; CPU-bound and fits 16 cores. Concern: verification queries can be slow, so scale the models down

title: DepCache: A KV Cache Management Framework for GraphRAG with Dependency Attention
note: KV-cache management framework for GraphRAG LLM inference - cache policy inside an inference engine - fits a single GPU with a small model

title: Bespoke OLAP: Synthesizing Workload-Specific One-size-fits-one Database Engines
note: LLM-driven synthesis of workload-specific OLAP engines compared against DuckDB and Umbra; a learned or LLM-based system-generation loop that runs entirely in user space. Concern: needs a paid LLM API and long synthesis loops

title: Mil: Cost-guided Minimum Makespan Scheduling for Applications of Multiple LLMs
note: Makespan scheduling for offline multi-LLM applications with an inference simulator and processing-rate estimators. Concern: GPU allocation and parallelism selection assume several GPUs so only the simulator and a single-GPU scaled-down setting are reproducible

title: ApproxMLIR : Accuracy-Aware Compiler for Compound ML System
note: Accuracy-aware MLIR dialect and optimizer for compound AI systems; the whole toolchain is user-space and MLIR/LLVM can be built into HOME. Concern: needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR build since clang is not installed

title: The FastLanes Compression Layout: Decoding >100 Billion Integers per Second with Scalar Code
note: Bit-packing/compression layout decoded with auto-vectorizable scalar code; CPU-only C++. Concern: headline numbers are from AVX-512 and SVE machines, Zen3 gives AVX2 only

title: CrossPipe: Towards Optimal Pipeline Schedules for Cross-Datacenter Training
note: Solver-based and greedy pipeline-schedule optimizer with an execution engine that separates scheduling from execution, so the schedule optimization can be studied in simulation. Concern: hardware evaluation used 4x GH200, so only the solver/simulation half is reproducible here

title: Optimizing Block Skipping for High-Dimensional Data with Learned Adaptive Curve
note: Learned space-filling curve for data layout and block skipping; user space

title: LogGrep: Fast and Cheap Cloud Log Storage by Exploiting both Static and Runtime Patterns
note: Log compression plus query engine, plain C, single machine, no root. Actively maintained repo with an explicit EuroSys'23 artifact statement plus a companion LogGrep-zstd repo. Concern - the Alibaba log datasets used in the paper may need to be sourced or substituted.

title: Pilot Execution: Simulating Failure Recovery In Situ for Production Distributed Systems
note: Pure user-space runtime library plus analysis framework that dry-runs recovery actions in distributed systems - target systems (HDFS, ZooKeeper, Kafka class) can be run as multiple processes on one host. Concern - some case studies assume production-scale deployments.

title: One-Size-Fits-None: Understanding and Enhancing Slow-Fault Tolerance in Modern Distributed Systems
note: Artifact is the Xinda fail-slow injection pipeline plus the ADR adaptive-threshold library (adr/ directory in the repo); both are user-space, and slow-I/O injection uses CharybdeFS, a FUSE filesystem - FUSE is usable on this machine. Concerns: the repo ships CloudLab/Ansible deployment scripts and the six target systems (Cassandra, HDFS, Kafka, etcd, ...) are normally multi-node, so everything must be collapsed to multiple processes on one host; some harness pieces assume Docker, which is not installed.

title: SHiFT: An Efficient, Flexible Search Engine for Transfer Learning
note: Search engine over a pretrained-model zoo with cost models and caching; one A5000 suffices for the small models. Concern: full model zoo plus datasets is a large download

title: Going Green for Less Green: Optimizing the Cost of Reducing Cloud Carbon Emissions
note: GAIA carbon-aware batch scheduler; the artifact ships both an AWS ParallelCluster driver and a pure simulation interface, and the simulator alone reproduces most figures on one machine.

title: TensorSocket: Shared Data Loading for Deep Learning Training
note: shared data loader for collocated deep-learning training jobs - directly targets CPU-side input-pipeline bottlenecks - concern: paper exploits GPU-GPU interconnects - single-GPU collocation still demonstrable

title: Blitzcrank: Fast Semantic Compression for In-memory Online Transaction Processing
note: semantic compression for in-memory OLTP row stores; user-space C++ with TPC-C evaluation

title: Dias: Dynamic Rewriting of Pandas Code
note: User-space runtime that rewrites pandas code at execution time; pure Python/CPU, no root

title: Relax: Composable Abstractions for End-to-End Dynamic Machine Learning
note: Relax cross-level compiler abstraction with first-class symbolic shapes, upstreamed into Apache TVM - user-space, one GPU is enough

title: Roadrunner: Accelerating Data Delivery to WebAssembly-Based Serverless Functions
note: Rust sidecar shim doing near-zero-copy, serialization-free transfer between WasmEdge VMs using vmsplice/splice - ordinary unprivileged syscalls, no eBPF, no kernel module, single host. Inter-function latency and throughput microbenchmarks are the headline results and are reproducible locally. Concern: the artifact packages functions as OCI bundles for containerd and the paper positions it inside Knative/OpenFaaS; with no Docker or root, the shim would have to be driven directly or through rootless tooling built in $HOME.

title: TUNA: Tuning Unstable and Noisy Cloud Applications
note: ML-based outlier removal and denoising to make autotuning converge under performance variability; the tuner is user-space Python and the noise characterization needs only timers. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper's premise is cloud noise, and this shared single machine has a different noise profile, which is itself a testable hypothesis

title: SVFusion: A CPU-GPU Co-Processing Architecture for Large-Scale Real-Time Vector Search
note: CPU GPU disk co-processing architecture with workload-aware GPU-memory caching and CUDA multi-stream coordination; explicitly designed around limited GPU memory so it scales to one A5000

title: Enabling Tensor Language Model to Assist in Generating High-Performance Tensor Programs for Deep Learning
note: Language model that emits tensor-program schedules for TVM/Ansor - learned component inside a compiler. Runs on one GPU. Concern - fine-tuning the tensor language model is compute heavy so a scaled-down model or released checkpoints would be needed

title: Moving on From Group Commit: Autonomous Commit Enables High Throughput and Low Latency on NVMe SSDs
note: Commit/logging protocol tuned for NVMe SSD parallelism; user-space DBMS change, machine has NVMe. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/latency .

title: Compiling Loop-Based Nested Parallelism for Irregular Workloads
note: LLVM/NOELLE compiler plus user-space heartbeat scheduling runtime for nested parallelism on a multicore CPU; 16C/32T Threadripper is a reasonable target. Concern - the interrupt-based rollforward variant may need a signal/timer path that should be checked.

title: Optimizing Video Analytics with Declarative Model Relationships
note: Declarative video analytics that exploits model-relationship hints to trade accuracy for speed; single-GPU inference, AE-reviewed artifact repo

title: Automatic Tracing in Task-Based Runtime Systems
note: Apophenia auto-traces dependence analysis in a user-space task-based runtime (Legion); runs on one node - concern: evaluated on supercomputers and no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: DPack: Efficiency-Oriented Privacy Budget Scheduling
note: Privacy budget scheduler formulated as a knapsack problem and evaluated purely in simulation on a synthetic workload derived from an Alibaba cluster trace; CPU only. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - none significant, which also means gains must come from better algorithms rather than systems engineering

title: Model Checking Guided Testing for Distributed Systems
note: Mocket drives a TLA+ model checker to guide implementation-level testing of Java distributed systems (ZooKeeper and similar); everything runs as ordinary local JVM processes, no cluster needed. Concern - Java must be installed in user space, and state-space exploration time is the main cost, which is itself a plausible improvement target.

title: TGLite: A Lightweight Programming Framework for Continuous-Time Temporal Graph Neural Networks
note: Lightweight framework and TBlock abstraction for continuous-time temporal GNNs; single-GPU evaluation against TGL.

title: Towards Ideal Temporal Graph Neural Networks: Evaluations and Conclusions after 10,000 GPU Hours
note: Unified TGNN design-space search framework with released code; each configuration is single-GPU. Concern: the published study consumed 10000 GPU hours so only a scaled-down slice of the space is feasible

title: High-Performance Query Processing with NVMe Arrays: Spilling without Killing Performance
note: Out-of-memory hash operators and spilling compression on NVMe; machine has 2 NVMe devices so a scaled-down study is possible - concern: paper uses a larger NVMe array

title: EVStore: Storage and Caching Capabilities for Scaling Embedding Tables in Deep Recommendation Systems
note: Multi-layer embedding-table cache for DLRM inference - single node CPU/GPU user space  cache admission/eviction policy is a clean improvement target

title: Practical and Asymptotically Optimal Quantization of High-Dimensional Vectors in Euclidean Space for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Extended RaBitQ quantization for ANN; CPU SIMD, single machine

title: ChainedFilter: Combining Membership Filters by Chain Rule
note: Composition of membership filters (Bloom/cuckoo/perfect hashing) with LSM and other storage use cases; CPU only

title: Hardware-Efficient Data Imputation through DBMS Extensibility
note: shape-wise microbatching execution model inside the BOSS DBMS kernel; user-space C++

title: MCTuner: Spatial Decomposition-Enhanced Database Tuning via LLM-Guided Exploration
note: LLM-guided spatial decomposition for database knob tuning - ML-based tuning - local DBMS plus an LLM endpoint - concern: no repo located

title: HealthServe: A Public Health-Aware Inference Framework
note: Health- and carbon-aware scheduling for LLM inference across geo-distributed GPU pools. Concern: the paper evaluates a heterogeneous multi-region cluster, so a single-node reproduction has to run the scheduler against simulated regions; the optimizer itself is user-space Python

title: RoarGraph: A Projected Bipartite Graph for Efficient Cross-Modal Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: cross-modal ANN graph index; single-machine memory-bound C++. Concern: ANN indexing is a borderline fit for the topic table

title: Gopher: Efficient Dynamic Graph Pattern Mining via DAG-Driven Execution
note: Dynamic graph pattern mining engine with DAG-based common subexpression elimination - CPU-only user-space system that fits 16 cores and 125 GB RAM. Not in the AE results list, no repo found

title: DiffForward: On Balancing Forwarding Traffic for Modern Cloud Block Services via Differentiated Forwarding
note: Separates burst from stable write traffic at the client of a cloud block service and routes burst traffic round-robin into a decentralized log store to remove the proxy-layer imbalance. Official code released by the first author (Python, client/server/manager/utils). In-topic as a storage-engine/IO-path policy that is trace-driven. Concerns - the system is inherently multi-role (client, proxy servers, distributed log store) so on one host it can only be run as co-located processes; no README or build instructions in the repo and no open-access PDF found, so the burst-detection mechanism would have to be reconstructed from the ACM DL version

title: DOGI: Data Placement with Oracle-Guided Insights for Log-Structured Systems
note: Lightweight ML predicts block invalidation time to guide data placement and cut GC write amplification; the main evaluation is a simulator plus a near-optimal oracle baseline (NoDaP), which runs fine on CPU with no root. Concern: the secondary prototype runs on a zoned (ZNS) device, which this machine does not have - the simulation track is the usable one.

title: Calcspar: A Contract-Aware LSM Store for Cloud Storage with Low Latency Spikes
note: LSM key-value store (RocksDB-derived): fluctuation-aware cache plus a congestion-aware IOPS allocator - user-space C++, no root, and LSM stores are explicitly in the storage topic. Concerns: the premise is Amazon EBS IOPS-contract latency variance, so reproducing it locally requires emulating cloud-storage latency (e.g. an injection layer or a FUSE shim over local NVMe - /dev/fuse is usable here); AE badge is Available only, so build effort is unverified.

title: IcebergHT: High Performance PMEM Hash Tables Through Stability and Low Associativity
note: Stability plus low-associativity hash table design; artifact released. Concern: headline results target Optane PMEM which this machine lacks, and the build links libpmem - only the DRAM configuration is reproducible

title: AirIndex: Versatile Index Tuning Through Data and Storage
note: I/O-aware hierarchical index builder; single-node storage profiling on NVMe, user space only

title: GiPH: Generalizable Placement Learning for Adaptive Heterogeneous Computing
note: Learned device-placement policy evaluated on synthetic task graphs and simulated heterogeneous device clusters - the whole evaluation is a simulator plus a GNN policy that trains on one GPU - concern - the simulator fidelity is the main threat to any improvement claim

title: The Holon Approach for Simultaneously Tuning Multiple Components in a Self-Driving Database Management System with Machine Learning via Synthesized Proto-Actions
note: holistic RL tuning across knobs, indexes and query hints on PostgreSQL. Concern: tuning runs are long

title: PIT - Optimization of Dynamic Sparse Deep Learning Models via Permutation Invariant Transformation
note: GPU sparse-kernel compiler/runtime for dynamic sparsity; the mechanism is per-GPU and Ampere sm_86 is supported by the CUDA kernels. Concerns - the AE README asks for 8x V100-32GB or 1x A100-80GB and 200-700 GB disk, so models must be scaled down to fit 24 GB and 257 GB; reproduction is shipped as a Docker image that has to be ported to conda; no FP8 paths involved so Ampere is otherwise fine. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/pit_artifact .

title: Improving Time Series Data Compression in Apache IoTDB
note: Homomorphic compression in Apache IoTDB - querying directly on compressed data; single-node JVM system

title: BACH: Bridging Adjacency List and CSR Format using LSM-Trees for HGTAP Workloads
note: LSM-tree whose compaction transforms the data layout; disk-based single-node storage engine

title: STile: Searching Hybrid Sparse Formats for Sparse Deep Learning Operators Automatically
note: Sparse-format search for sparse DL operators - an ML compiler/codegen artifact; single GPU (Ampere) is the paper's setting

title: ExecuTorch - A Unified PyTorch Solution to Run ML Models On-Device
note: PyTorch-native on-device runtime - memory planning, operator/backend registry, quantization workflows are all user-space and buildable from source. Concerns: most of the evaluation is on phones, NPUs and MCUs that are unavailable; only the portable/XNNPACK/CUDA backends can be exercised here

title: Helix: Serving Large Language Models over Heterogeneous GPUs and Network via Max-Flow
note: Max-flow model placement plus request scheduling for LLM serving; concern: real runs need a heterogeneous 24-42 GPU cluster, but the released artifact contains a cluster simulator that fits one machine

title: AdaGen: Workload-Adaptive Cluster Scheduler for Latency-Optimal LLM Inference Serving
note: Workload-adaptive scheduling of compute layouts for LLM serving instances - request scheduling logic that can be driven by traces or a small number of local instances. Concern: multi-instance cluster target, no code found

title: LPO: Discovering Missed Peephole Optimizations with Large Language Models
note: LLM proposes LLVM peephole rewrites that Alive2 verifies; entirely user-space and CPU-bound. Concern: needs an LLM API budget and is closer to compilers than to classic systems

title: ChainKV: A Semantics-Aware Key-Value Store for Ethereum System
note: Semantics-aware LSM key-value store for Ethereum state; single-node NVMe

title: Parrotfish: Parametric Regression for Optimizing Serverless Functions
note: Online parametric-regression rightsizing of serverless function memory; the learner itself is a small Python 3.12 package that fits the machine trivially and is still actively maintained. Concern: the measured exploration loop invokes real AWS Lambda (or GCP) functions, which env.md's "single machine only" does not provide - the project would have to drive the regressor from recorded duration-vs-memory sweeps or a local function emulator, which is a real risk.

title: Hourglass: An Adaptive Range Filter with Lightweight Hybrid Encoding
note: adaptive range filter for key-value stores - small self-contained C/C++ artifact - concern: no public repo located by search

title: SpecProto: A Parallelizing Compiler for Speculative Decoding of Large Protocol Buffers Data
note: Parallelizing compiler for Protobuf decoding; CPU-only artifact that targets 16 physical cores which this machine has

title: Rainbow: Risk-aware Index Benefit Estimation Facing Out Of Distribution Workloads
note: risk-aware learned index-benefit estimation under workload drift - learned DBMS component - concern: no abstract or repo found - may target a commercial engine

title: Sharpen the Spec, Cut the Code: A Case for Generative File System with SYSSPEC
note: Best Paper + Distinguished Artifact. SPECFS runs in userspace via FUSE (confirmed in the paper and in the artifact appendix, which lists fuse/libfuse-dev as the only system requirement) - /dev/fuse and setuid fusermount3 are available on this machine. Concern: the generation pipeline needs an external LLM API key (Gemini or DeepSeek), i.e. network access and some API spend.

title: Fast Inference for Probabilistic Graphical Models
note: Parallel user-space inference engine for probabilistic graphical models, CPU-only C++ with OpenMP; builds and runs entirely in user space on 16 cores, clear speedup metric to improve

title: OctoSketch: Enabling Real-Time, Continuous Network Monitoring over Multiple Cores
note: Change-based continuous aggregation that scales sketches across many cores; the repo has separate CPU, DPDK and XDP implementations, and the CPU variant is plain multi-threaded user-space C++ that suits a 16-core machine. Concerns: the DPDK and eBPF-XDP variants need root and eBPF (blocked), so only the CPU variant is usable; packet traces (for example CAIDA) must be obtained separately and the no-DPDK setup changes the achievable packet rates.

title: Shockwave: Fair and Efficient Cluster Scheduling for Dynamic Adaptation in Machine Learning
note: ML cluster scheduler whose main evaluation arm is a trace-driven discrete-event simulator that runs entirely on one CPU machine - Concern: the physical-cluster half of the paper used dozens of GPUs so only the simulation results are reproducible or improvable here

title: Modeling Shifting Workloads for Learned Database Systems
note: Training-set construction for learned database components under workload shift. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search

title: Orion: Interference-aware Fine-grained GPU Sharing for ML Applications
note: Intercepts CUDA kernel launches in user space and schedules operators from co-located clients on one GPU. Single-GPU by design and the whole point is contention on one device. Concern - built against a specific PyTorch/CUDA pairing, so pinning a working toolchain on driver 535 / CUDA 11.8 is the main build risk

title: Select Edges Wisely: Monotonic Path Aware Graph Layout Optimization for Disk-based ANN Search
note: Disk-resident ANN graph layout optimization - contribution is disk locality and I/O reduction. Concern: sits between storage and vector indexing, audit should decide

title: Efficient Concurrent Updates to Persistent Randomized Binary Search Trees
note: Concurrent multi-version in-memory search tree for multicore - user-space C++ concurrency work

title: Understanding Robustness Issues of Updatable Learned Indexes: [Experiments & Analysis]
note: experimental study of robustness of updatable learned indexes - reusable benchmark harness over open-source learned indexes - concern: artifact URL not located
